anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 anchor is a finite 3D raycast and occlusion problem: the solver rotates a 5x5x3 view, mines four visible targets, and manages lava, support and durability constraints. Clockbeat L4 instead exposes an 8x8 2D map whose state changes every beat, with three sentries that chase, shield or strike, two hits required per sentry, and only three player hearts. The voxel task has more 3D viewpoint and motor-precision demands, but Clockbeat adds temporal enemy behavior, expiring actions and state-dependent combat, so the current Clockbeat profile is above this low anchor on the relevant decision problem.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 anchor requires active cursor vision to reveal a constellation target and select it within a radius amid decoys, but there is one primary target selection and no beat-driven adversarial state transition. Clockbeat L4 requires repeated timed actions while the visible enemy roster and map evolve, and each combat decision changes later pursuit and attack states. It is therefore above the L2 target-selection problem even though Constellation Hunt has more continuous pointer positioning.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 anchor is continuous physics and motor control: the player manages momentum, friction, walls, wells, three ordered lamps and a final cup. Clockbeat L4 is less demanding in continuous cursor precision, but it has an adversarial multi-agent state, phase-dependent combat, a one-action-per-beat constraint and an expiring action window. These are different difficulty axes; source supports Clockbeat above the L2 anchor and in the L4 band, but does not empirically prove a strict ordering against every aspect of Gyro L3.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 anchor has an 18x11 maze, five barriers/gates, hidden orientation, scanner-dependent information and a 48-to-105-roll route. Clockbeat L4 has a smaller, fully visible map and only three sentries, but its beat clock expires inputs, enemy phases change over time, and combat plus health make each route decision state-dependent. The two tasks are comparable L4-scale stateful problems on different axes; Blind Dice has longer hidden-information memory while Clockbeat has tighter temporal action control.

Each accepted swap changes the later board and branching plan. Clockbeat L4 has dependent combat and timing, but its visible deterministic board has a shorter route and no exact-score or cascade search; it is below this L5 reference.

visible_baseline_solution: A screenshot-only solver must read the visible 8x8 map, walls, player, stair, enemy positions, hearts, roster roles/phases and the beat indicator. It must wind the clock, choose one directional action or wait during the first 1150 ms of each 1800 ms beat, and observe consecutive frames because crawlers and hoppers move at beat boundaries while lancers can expose an adjacent strike phase. Moving into an enemy is combat, but a hopper's shield phase can block the hit; each of the three sentries needs two successful hits. The solver must plan around walls and changing enemy positions, avoid losing all three hearts, and finally enter the stair after all enemies are dead. The replay must remain within the beat/time bounds, use the selected input source, and end with the exact winning state; a private-state route solver is implementation evidence only, not the screenshot-only behavior being measured.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current L4/full task is a multi-step, state-changing temporal combat problem. It is materially above the approved L1 voxel extraction and L2 single-target cursor tasks, broadly comparable to the approved L4 Blind Dice stateful route, and below the approved L5 exact-change cascade search. The L3 Gyro comparison is a tradeoff rather than a source-proven total ordering: Gyro has harder continuous motor physics, while Clockbeat has more adversarial timing and combat dependencies. The approved L4 label is therefore a defensible fit, with no source-supported profile relabel.

findings.claim: The simplified mechanic does not visibly spell out the WAIT action: it renders the button glyph as a dot, while only the aria-label says WAIT. The source therefore does not by itself establish that a screenshot-only user receives the same explicit wait instruction as full mode.
findings.causal_explanation: The control contract says simplified mode has direction buttons and a wait button, but the browser's simplified button map renders WAIT as '·'; full mode instead shows the explicit 'ARROWS / WASD · SPACE TO WAIT' legend. The materializer can place interaction-specific natural-language text in task metadata, but the supplied source does not show whether that text is visible in the screenshot task surface. If it is not, simplified users must infer the dot's effect or use an unlabeled control, changing information burden even though action effects and grading remain equivalent.

evidence.explanation: The interaction contract distinguishes simplified direction buttons from full arrows/WASD/Space.
The rendered simplified WAIT control uses the glyph '·', while its aria label is WAIT; the same line includes the full-mode keyboard legend.
Interaction-specific natural-language instructions are written as task metadata, but this path does not prove that they are screenshot-visible during browser play.
The generated public prompt is the generic objective, so it does not itself identify the simplified WAIT glyph.

findings.recommended_action: Verify the actual screenshot/task-description surface for every simplified configuration. If no visible instruction names WAIT, label the button visibly or expose the selected interaction-specific instruction before human/agent calibration; keep the world and grader changes otherwise unchanged.

verdict.concise_summary: Keep Clockbeat Catacomb at the approved L4/full baseline and retain all five ordered difficulty profiles in both interaction modes. Source comparison supports L1 through L5 as active state-dependent combat changes, places L4 alongside Blind Dice Courier L4 and below Exact-Change Candy Cascade L5, and finds no source-proven difficulty reversal or inactive profile knob. Treat the simplified WAIT label as a low-severity visible-instruction caveat pending the parent's runtime check.
